messages:
olivia (Customer): Hey team — running into a weird issue with the batch rerank endpoint. We send 5 queries in one request and each query has a different number of candidates (10, 8, 12, 4, 6). The response returns a flat scores array but it looks like the scores are misaligned with candidates for query 2 and 4. Some top candidates for query 2 are scoring like they belong to query 3.

alice (Support): Sorry you're hitting that — can you paste the original request body (redact any PII) and the response you got? Also which SDK / API version are you on?

olivia (Customer): Here's a minimal repro (redacted). We're using the REST API directly v1.2.1.

olivia (Customer): ```
POST /v1/rerank/batch HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "queries": [
    {"id":"q1","text":"find foo"},
    {"id":"q2","text":"search bar"},
    {"id":"q3","text":"lookup baz"},
    {"id":"q4","text":"query qux"},
    {"id":"q5","text":"get quux"}
  ],
  "candidates": [
    /* flattened candidates in expected per-query order */
    /* 10 for q1, 8 for q2, 12 for q3, 4 for q4, 6 for q5 */
    "c1","c2",...
  ],
  "candidate_counts": [10,8,12,4,6],
  "options": {"score_normalization": "none"}
}
```

olivia (Customer): Response (trimmed):
```json
{
  "scores": [0.12, 0.43, 0.99, 0.02, ... /* length 40 */],
  "request_id": "r-abc123",
  "status": "ok"
}
```

olivia (Customer): But when we map scores to candidates using the provided candidate_counts, some top hits for q2 are nonsense — e.g., candidate indexes 10-17 should be q2 but the top scored ones match q3 results.

alice (Support): Got it. Two quick asks: (1) can you confirm the length of the scores array equals sum(candidate_counts) (should be 40 here)? (2) If you set candidate_counts to equal and pad candidates to same length, does behavior change?

olivia (Customer): Yes length is 40. We tried padding to equal length (12 each) and it *seems* to align correctly. So this may be triggered when candidate lists are variable-length.

mike (SRE): @alice assigning. We saw a deploy to rerank flattening logic yesterday evening (deploy-bot: 1764119000). Any chance that introduced an index-shift bug? Also noticed some latency spikes around 1764123000 — could be a race.

rerank-bot: deploy 1764118920 by devin (ML Eng) -> rollout 30% -> active.

devin (ML Eng): Thanks for the repro @olivia, and ping @mike. The flattening code was refactored to optimize memory copying across batched requests. Hypothesis: when candidate_counts has variable lengths we might be computing offsets incorrectly in the fast path. I'll dig in.

alice (Support): In the meantime, can you try one of two mitigations: (A) split into separate rerank calls per query, or (B) send padded candidate arrays and include candidate_counts so we can map correctly? Customer tried B and saw improvement.

olivia (Customer): We don't want to do per-query calls — that kills latency/throughput for us. Padding works as a short-term workaround but doubles payload for some queries. Is there any billing/usage impact we should worry about?

jen (Billing): Padding could inflate billable units if the billing metric counts per-candidate evaluation rather than per-actual candidate. Need to confirm. @alice @mike - can we get clarity on whether rerank billing is based on total candidates submitted or on actual non-padding markers?

mike (SRE): I'll check metrics for the customer's request_id r-abc123 and also search logs for offset computations in the rerank service around that request. If this is a rollout bug, we can roll back the change quickly.

devin (ML Eng): Quick repro script that reproduces the misalignment for us locally (python requests):
```python
import requests
url = "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank/batch"
body = {
  "queries": [ {"id":"q1"},{"id":"q2"},{"id":"q3"},{"id":"q4"},{"id":"q5"} ],
  "candidates": ["c1"]*10 + ["c2"]*8 + ["c3"]*12 + ["c4"]*4 + ["c5"]*6,
  "candidate_counts": [10,8,12,4,6]
}
res = requests.post(url, json=body, headers={"Authorization":"Bearer REDACTED"})
print(res.status_code, res.json())
```

devin (ML Eng): When I run locally against the canary build, I see the scores array but offsets are applied as if candidate_counts were [10,12,8,4,6] i.e., a swap between q2 and q3 in the fast-path.

alice (Support): Thanks @devin. @olivia if you can share the full request_id / a second failing request_id that'd help. We'll also ask SRE to consider a rollback if canary reproduces the issue.

olivia (Customer): I can share a second id: r-abc456. Sending via Support DM now.

mike (SRE): Confirmed logs for r-abc123 and r-abc456 show unexpected offset computation results in the optimized path at host rerank-07. Rolling back the canary and forcing rerank to use safe path for now.

rerank-bot: rollback 1764118920 by mike -> completed at 1764123465.

devin (ML Eng): I've pushed a hotfix branch which fixes the offset computation when candidate_counts are variable — PR #4321. Plan: run integration tests, merge, and redeploy canary after verifying.

jen (Billing): FYI — padding increases candidate count in payload; billing is charged per-evaluated candidate. For the customer's padded workaround, billing will reflect the padded total. We'll coordinate credits if needed for this incident.

alice (Support): Next steps: (1) we've rolled back the risky optimization and routes are on safe path (mike) (2) devin will patch and redeploy canary with tests (devin) (3) support to follow up with customer about credits/impact (alice/jen) (4) customer to keep us posted if you see anything after the rollback (olivia).

olivia (Customer): Thanks all — rollback reduced the symptom immediately. We'll hold off on padding now. Please keep us posted on timing for the patched canary. Appreciate the quick action. :heart:

alice (Support): We'll update this thread when the fix lands in canary and again when it's fully rolled out. Closing loop here but keeping thread open until the fix is GA'd.

devin (ML Eng): Patch merged to main in PR #4321, canary will start at 30% in ~20m. I'll post results.

mike (SRE): Monitoring for regressions; no further latency spikes observed after rollback (so far).

alice (Support): Thread note: repro steps and scripts saved to internal support case #SUP-2026.

olivia (Customer): Thanks — closing on our side once you confirm the canary looks good.
